title: Cost of a 20' / 40' container to Angola | MB Fret Services
description: Understand what drives the cost of a 20' or 40' container between France and Angola for your business shipments and international moves: container type, ports, FCL/LCL, seasonality, and included services. Typical configurations, practical advice and a method to build a realistic budget without unpleasant surprises.
hero_h1: Cost of a 20' / 40' container to Angola
hero_intro: There is no single “catalogue price” for a container: the budget depends on actual volume, container type, departure and arrival ports, season, and which services are included (pre/post-carriage, customs, insurance). This guide helps you understand the main price drivers so you can build a realistic budget for your shipments to Angola.

sections.h2: Why there is no single catalogue price for a container
p: Sea freight rates are volatile: they vary by season, carrier capacity, ports of loading and discharge, container type and cargo profile. A price shown out of context often looks simple, but rarely reflects your real project (personal effects, vehicles, B2B cargo, tight deadlines, etc.).

The goal is not to find a universal price, but to obtain a structured quote that breaks down cost elements (freight, surcharges, THC, pre/post-carriage, customs, insurance) so you can compare and decide on the basis of total delivered cost.

sections.h2: Key parameters that drive your container cost
ul: Container type: 20' or 40', Dry, High Cube, Reefer, Open Top, Flat Rack… each setup has a different cost structure.
Departure and arrival ports: Le Havre, Fos, Antwerp, Rotterdam to Luanda, with varying surcharges depending on trade lanes and carriers.
FCL vs LCL service: a full container reserved for you, or LCL groupage shared with other shippers.
Seasonality and capacity: peak seasons, holidays, port congestion and strikes have a direct impact on rate levels.
Cargo nature: standard, dangerous goods (IMO), reefer, bulky, sensitive or high-value cargo.
Additional services: pickup, handling, palletization, temporary storage, export/import customs, ad valorem cargo insurance.

p: The examples below are not price lists, but common configurations we handle on the France → Angola trade. They provide typical budget scenarios to show how total delivered cost is built in practice, without publishing specific amounts.
ul: Example 1 – small LCL volume (3–5 pallets of personal effects or B2B cargo): groupage from a French or Benelux port to Luanda. You pay only for the volume you occupy in the shared container.

Example 2 – full international move in a 20' FCL with personal effects + possibly one vehicle: a sealed container managed end-to-end, often including pickup, stuffing, freight, export customs and insurance based on declared value.
Example 3 – 40' FCL for large B2B flows: pallets, spare parts, consumables, sometimes a machine or vehicle, with a regular transport pattern and focus on rate stability over time.

p: Towards Luanda, access to the port and pre/post-carriage solutions from France or Benelux ports (Antwerp, Rotterdam) are key price drivers. The market is very sensitive to cargo type (vehicles, moves, B2B lots) and the quality of port services.

Projects combining personal effects, boxes, furniture and sometimes one or two vehicles in a single 20' or 40' container require precise study: stuffing plan, securing, insured value and Angolan customs requirements need to be considered right from quote stage.

sections.h2: FCL vs LCL: direct impact on your budget
p: Below roughly 13–15 m³, LCL groupage is usually more attractive: you pay only for the volume used, with a bit more handling and sometimes slightly longer transit times.
Above that range, 20' or 40' FCL containers often become the most relevant option: lower cost per m³, fewer handlings, and better risk control for full moves, vehicles and sensitive cargo.
ul: LCL: suitable for small volumes, market tests or occasional flows. Very flexible, but requires solid export packing.
FCL: essential for full international moves, vehicles/motorbikes, machinery and regular high-value flows.

sections.h2: How to obtain a clear, usable quote
ol: List your volumes (m³ or dimensions + weight), cargo types (personal effects, merchandise, vehicles) and precise destination (city/country).
Specify whether you are considering LCL or FCL, or if you want advice on the best setup.
Indicate which services you expect: pickup, palletization, container loading, customs clearance, insurance, possible delivery at destination.
Request a quote broken down by cost element (freight, surcharges, THC, pre/post-carriage, customs, insurance) with a clearly stated validity period.
Compare FCL/LCL scenarios on total delivered cost rather than on a single “port-to-port” rate.

ul: Chasing a simplistic “all-purpose price” found online without checking what is really included.
Comparing quotes that do not cover the same scope (port-to-port vs door-to-door, with or without customs/insurance).
Underestimating the impact of seasonality, congestion and temporary surcharges on some ports.
Ignoring export packing and insurance, which determine how well your goods are protected if something goes wrong.

faq.q: I’m a company: how is the price of a 20' or 40' container for my B2B flows France–Angola calculated?
faq.a: For B2B shipments, the cost of a container depends on container type (20'/40', dry, high cube, reefer), departure/arrival ports, seasonality, cargo nature and which services are included (pre/post-carriage, handling, customs, insurance). Your budget quickly runs into several thousand euros. Rather than giving a single price, we break down each cost element (freight, surcharges, THC, pre/post, customs, insurance) so you can clearly understand and control your total delivered cost.

faq.q: I’m planning an international move to Angola: what budget should I expect for a 20' or 40' container?
faq.a: There is no one-size-fits-all rate, because the price depends on your actual volume (personal effects, furniture, boxes), whether a vehicle is included and which services you need (pickup, packing, loading, customs, insurance). A full move in a 20' or 40' FCL typically represents a budget of several thousand euros. The most efficient approach is to share your project (estimated volume, departure city, destination, required services) so we can build a realistic, itemised budget with you.

faq.q: Why can two container quotes look very different?
faq.a: Because they may not cover the same scope: some are purely port-to-port, while others include pickup, customs formalities, insurance and sometimes delivery at destination. We systematically clarify what is included and what remains at your charge so you can compare offers on a like‑for‑like basis and avoid misunderstandings.

faq.q: Is LCL always cheaper than a 20' FCL?
faq.a: For small volumes (a few cubic metres), LCL groupage is generally more cost-effective. But as soon as your volume increases or you combine moves, vehicles and cargo in a single project, a 20' FCL can become more attractive in cost per m³ and in securing your supply chain. We always compare LCL/FCL scenarios before making a recommendation.

faq.q: Can we combine a move and a vehicle in the same container?
faq.a: Yes, subject to feasibility and the regulatory constraints of the destination country. This type of project has a direct impact on the budget (space, weight, insurance, customs), which is why a tailor-made quote is far more relevant than a generic price. We work with you to build the best setup to combine personal effects and vehicle in a single container when appropriate.

faq.q: How can we avoid unpleasant price surprises (THC, demurrage, etc.)?
faq.a: By requesting a quote broken down by cost element and clarifying quote validity, storage conditions, free time at port and each party’s responsibilities. As your freight forwarder, our role is to help you anticipate these potential extra costs and clearly frame the scope of services from the outset.
